about: The context quiz: questions the head trader (and the risk manager) must answer from their prompts alone, each the agreed rule it checks and the phrase in the skills that states it. Run on demand (scripts/context-quiz.js), never in CI: it calls a model. A changed key or question needs a reason in the pull request, as a golden does.
answerFormat: Answer from your instructions only. First line: ANSWER: <one line>. Then at most 3 lines of why.
unsure: it depends|unsure|not sure|unclear|ambiguous|can't tell|cannot tell|depends on

questions.text: The 4h trend is up and the 1h trend is down. Can you take a long? A short?
questions.rule: no side when the 4h and 1h disagree: never counter
questions.anchor: each trending 4h or 1h your way, neither against

questions.text: The 4h and 1h both range. What sets the side?
questions.rule: both ranging: the 15m trend and the declared trend
questions.anchor: both ranging: the 15m and `Trend declared?` your way

questions.text: The 4h is down, the 1h down, and a 1h CHoCH up just printed at a level. Can you go long?
questions.rule: never against a trending 4h or 1h; a CHoCH against the bias is context
questions.anchor: A CHoCH against the bias is context, never a way in.

questions.text: Which timeframes set the bias?
questions.rule: the bias is the 4h and the 1h
questions.anchor: The bias (4h + 1h) sets the side

questions.text: Which timeframe is the setup read on?
questions.rule: the setup is the 15m (or a fired momentum_continuation)
questions.anchor: The setup is the 15m (or higher) reaction or break

questions.text: What is a 3m swing high for: a level to trade from, a target, or only where the stop goes?
questions.rule: a 3m swing is no level and no target, only where the stop goes
questions.anchor: A 3m swing is not a level and not a target.

questions.text: A 3m CHoCH up prints while the 15m setup has not formed. Is that a setup?
questions.rule: a 3m break is never the setup
questions.anchor: a 3m candle is no setup

questions.text: A 15m setup candle closed as a bearish engulfing; another closed as a strong full-body bear candle in its bottom third with no pattern name. Which is the stronger setup candle?
questions.rule: a candle is judged by its strength and close, never its pattern name
questions.anchor: a name adds no strength, the reaction reads who took control

questions.text: Where do levels come from?
questions.rule: levels: the 1h and higher, the session and day, the VWAP, the 15m swings; never the 3m
questions.anchor: Levels come from the 1h and higher, the session and day

questions.text: The 15m setup closed at a 1h level on the bias side. When do you enter?
questions.rule: the next 3m close times the entry; no 3m turn to wait for
questions.anchor: no 3m turn to wait for

questions.text: Do you need a 3m BOS or CHoCH before entering?
questions.rule: no 3m break is required
questions.anchor: no 3m turn or break to wait for

questions.text: No size fits under the cap with compose's stop. Do you tighten the stop?
questions.rule: stops are locked: skip, never a tighter stop
questions.anchor: pass, never a closer stop

questions.text: Where does the stop go?
questions.rule: compose places the stop one tick beyond the named level; never tighter; on the bracket
questions.anchor: The stop: compose places it one tick beyond the level your stop read

questions.text: Can you move the stop to breakeven because the trade feels done?
questions.rule: the stop moves only behind turned structure (the trail)
questions.anchor: You tighten it only behind

questions.text: The trade reaches 2R. Do you exit there?
questions.rule: at 2R nothing exits: the 2R order is cancelled, the stop locks and trails
questions.anchor: At 2R nothing exits

questions.text: Is the named 1h swing high your exit?
questions.rule: the trail exits; a level is context
questions.anchor: the 2R mark that arms the trail, not the exit

questions.text: In a prop attempt the account is healthy (balance at or above start, no loss streak). What size: the full verdict size, or less?
questions.rule: a healthy prop account takes the full verdict size
questions.anchor: Size in a prop attempt: the full verdict size, the code's number.

questions.text: The setup has one serious factor against it, in a prop attempt. What size: the full verdict size, or less?
questions.rule: in a prop attempt nothing halves
questions.anchor: In a prop attempt nothing halves

questions.text: The risk manager writes "Size: I'd go with 3 contracts given the stop" and "VERDICT: approve". Is that a trade?
questions.rule: a bare approval states no readable size: one restate of the Size and VERDICT lines, never a veto (roles-ran.js approvedSize)
questions.anchor: with no size on the line → unreadable
forbidden: (?<!\b(?:never|not|no|rather than|instead of|only)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:real\s+)?)(?<!\b(?:never|not|does not|doesn't|do not|don't)\s+(?:treat|count|read|take)\w*\s+(?:it|this|that)\s+as\s+a\s+)\bveto(?:e[sd])?\b(?!\s+(?:is\s+|was\s+)?(?:never|not)\b)(?!\s+(?:would be wrong|would never|does not|doesn't|never)\b)

questions.text: The setup fits only 2 contracts at the stop. What do you do?
questions.rule: fewer than the minimum (3) at the stop: skip, unless the code's floor stretch fits it
questions.anchor: Fewer than 3 (`min_contracts`) at the stop: skip

questions.text: Positions read flat, but a fill shows a long 9 and its bracket stop is working. Do you cancel the stop as a leftover?
questions.rule: a fill reported late: a stop is never a leftover while fills or an order's status show the position; keep it ([cancel-protection] refuses its cancel)
questions.anchor: A stop is never a leftover while fills or an order's status show the position, even if positions read flat: `[cancel-protection]` refuses it; keep it.

questions.text: In a prop attempt your compose record states 8 MNQ, but order_plan gives 5 MNQ for the entry. What size do you place?
questions.rule: the size comes from the size translation (order_plan's number), never the model's own
questions.anchor: size, and stop ticks come from the size translation (`order_plan` gives them)

questions.text: A 15m long-wick rejection at the prior RTH high, nothing else lines up. Take it on the reaction alone?
questions.rule: a reaction is context, never decided on alone: it needs other confirmation (the bias, the level, the count)
questions.anchor: Context, never the setup alone: it needs other confirmation.

questions.text: A 15m candle has a long upper wick above the prior RTH high but closes above the high. Rejection or acceptance?
questions.rule: the close decides acceptance, the wick measures the failed attempt: a close beyond the level is acceptance, never a rejection
questions.anchor: The close beats the wick: a long wick closing above is no rejection

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes back below it, its upper wick longer than its body and a third of its range (the briefing: long-wick rejection). Who took control?
questions.rule: a long-wick rejection after a high: the other side, the sellers, took control
questions.anchor: → sellers rejected higher prices

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes above it, its body 0.8 of its range. A sweep of the high or a breakout?
questions.rule: a close beyond with an engulfing or a body of 0.7 of the range or more is a breakout attempt, not a sweep
questions.anchor: the breaking side in control, not a sweep

questions.text: A 15m long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high, then the next 15m candle is a bearish engulfing closing lower. What does that second candle read?
questions.rule: a long-wick rejection, then an opposite engulfing closing lower: a confirmed rejection, on the second candle
questions.anchor: closing lower → sellers took over, confirmed

questions.text: A 15m candle trades above the prior RTH high and closes back below it with a bullish body and a short wick (the briefing: conflicting). Read it as sellers in control now?
questions.rule: a conflicting reaction is mixed evidence: it needs other confirmation (the count, or the next candle)
questions.anchor: → mixed: needs other confirmation (the count, or the next candle)

questions.text: A 15m doji at the prior RTH high (the briefing: stall). What decides who takes control?
questions.rule: a stall: the push stalled, the next candle decides
questions.anchor: → stalled; the next candle decides

questions.text: Two 15m long-wick rejections of a high (upper wick through it, closed back below): one at a pullback level with the 4h and 1h down, one with the 4h and 1h up. What side is each, and which can be taken?
questions.rule: the side is the candle's: both are the short side (a rejection of a high); only the first, with the 4h and 1h, can be taken; against the 4h + 1h the trend rule refuses the second (never counter)
questions.anchor: Side first, from the candle

questions.text: The last 4h candle is a long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high; the 15m candle at it reads plain. Which reaction is the stronger, and is it a trade on its own?
questions.rule: the reaction rules hold on every timeframe and a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's; a reaction is still context: it needs other confirmation
questions.anchor: a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's
required: \b(needs?|wants?|requires?)\s+(other|more)\s+confirmation\b|\bconfirmation\b|\bcontext\b|\bthe count\b|\bnot (a trade )?(on its own|alone|by itself)\b|\bneither( one)? is a trade\b|\bis not a trade\b
forbidden: \b(trade it|sell it|go short|enter now|stands on its own|tradeable on its own|(valid|good) trade (by itself|on its own))\b(?!\s+(only\s+)?(once|if|after(?! all)|when|until)\b)

questions.text: The 3m candle is a long-wick rejection of the prior RTH high, but the last 1h candle closed decisively beyond it (broke above). Short on the 3m rejection?
questions.rule: a higher frame's reaction is stronger confirmation than a lower one's: the 1h close beyond outweighs the 3m rejection; the 3m only times the entry and alone can be noise (wait)
questions.anchor: 3m only times the entry; alone it can be noise

questions.text: Two 15m long-wick rejections of a low (lower wick through it, closed back above): one at a pullback level with the 4h and 1h up, one with the 4h and 1h down. What side is each, and which can be taken?
questions.rule: the side is the candle's: both are the long side (a rejection of a low); only the first, with the 4h and 1h, can be taken; against the 4h + 1h the trend rule refuses the second (never counter)
questions.anchor: Side first, from the candle

questions.text: A 15m candle `rejected` the prior RTH high (traded above, closed back below), and its reaction reads plain. Did the other side take control — is it a rejection?
questions.rule: the `rejected` relation is only the fact; it is a rejection only when its reaction is a long-wick, engulfing or confirmed rejection; plain: no one took control, weak context only
questions.anchor: It is a rejection only when its reaction is a long-wick, engulfing or confirmed rejection
required: \b(not a rejection|no rejection|no one took control|nobody took control|weak|context|confirm\w*|by itself|alone|reaction decides)\b
forbidden: \b(short it|take the short|go short|sell it)\b(?!\s+(only\s+)?(once|if|after(?! all)|when|until)\b)

questions.text: A 15m candle `rejected` a level in your composed read and its reaction reads conflicting. Which skill do you read for what that means, and how?
questions.rule: the reaction read is candle-reading's, read from the index with skill_lookup (or the cycle's embedded copy); the gate requires it on a composed rejection or break
questions.anchor: - a composed read says a candle rejected a level, or a composed read says a candle broke a level, or a composed read says a level was swept: `candle-reading`

questions.text: In a prop attempt, momentum_continuation fired long on the BG side. Can you take it?
questions.rule: a cited setup (S2) is traded in the attempt: cite it in compose_check (trade_lifecycle's citedSetup), never a reason to pass for being a rules strategy
questions.anchor: A setup the prompt names in this attempt (S2): cite it in

questions.text: The fired setup's track record says no backtest recorded. Is that a reason to pass?
questions.rule: a missing track record is never a reason to pass or cut (trade_lifecycle and a cited setup have none)
questions.anchor: never a reason to pass or cut

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. Your plan said: scenario 1: P1 "15m rejected prior vah up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior VAH | PASS if it closes below it; reads: "15m rejected prior vah up". The 15m closed back above the prior VAH: the briefing lists "15m rejected prior vah up". Confirm or pass?
questions.rule: a closed candle that meets the scenario's TAKE conditions is confirmed: compose_check with the at-close reads
questions.anchor: A met TAKE is a confirm:

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. Your plan said: scenario 1: P1 "15m rejected prior vah up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior VAH | PASS if it closes below it; reads: "15m rejected prior vah up". The 15m closed below the prior VAH: the briefing does not list "15m rejected prior vah up". Confirm or pass?
questions.rule: a closed candle that does not meet the TAKE conditions: pass, with why
questions.anchor: A pass is the CYCLE RESULT, with why.
required: ^[\W_]*(pass\w*|skip\w*|no\b|nope|not\b|not met|take not met|confirm nothing|stand down|decline|do not|don'?t)

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. Your plan said: scenario 1: P1 "15m rejected prior vah up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior VAH | PASS if it closes below it; reads: "15m rejected prior vah up". You were sure of this plan and wrote that you would take it, but the 15m closed below the prior VAH: the briefing does not list "15m rejected prior vah up". Take it as planned?
questions.rule: anchoring trap: the plan said take, the candle did not meet TAKE: pass; the plan is never evidence
questions.anchor: a plan that said take is no reason to take

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. Your plan said: scenario 1: P1 "15m rejected prior vah up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior VAH | PASS if it closes below it; reads: "15m rejected prior vah up". Scenario 3 was: P2 "15m rejected prior poc up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior POC. The 15m closed below the prior VAH (scenario 1's PASS) but back above the prior POC: the briefing lists "15m rejected prior poc up". Is scenario 3 off the table because scenario 1 said pass?
questions.rule: opposite trap: the candle meets a different listed scenario's TAKE conditions: judge it from the facts, it may be taken
questions.anchor: a plan that said pass is no reason to pass.

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. Your plan said: scenario 1: P1 "15m rejected prior vah up" -> TAKE if the 15m closes back above the prior VAH | PASS if it closes below it; reads: "15m rejected prior vah up". The plan wrote the read as "15m rejected prior vah up, wick 4 pts"; the at-close facts show the rejection with a 1 pt wick. Which do you compose with: the plan's read or the at-close facts?
questions.rule: the plan is never evidence: compose with the reads as the at-close facts give them
questions.anchor: with the reads as the at-close facts give them (not as the plan wrote them)

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. The briefing's Setups to check: "15m rejected prior poc up" (long; setup candle: hammer, close top third); the setup still stands: no confirming read needed. The trend rule allows a long. Your plan said: scenario 2: P3 "15m rejected prior poc up" (a standing scenario: its line fired "whatever its range, volume and close") -> TAKE if its reads compose at the close | PASS if compose_check refuses it; reads: "15m rejected prior poc up". The closing 3m closed below the 15m setup candle's low, and compose_check at the close refused it: the stop is not on the losing side of the entry. Confirm or pass?
questions.rule: a standing scenario: compose_check refusing it is the pass
questions.anchor: compose_check refusing is the pass

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. The briefing's Setups to check: "15m rejected prior poc up" (long; setup candle: hammer, close top third); the setup still stands: no confirming read needed. The trend rule allows a long. Your plan said: scenario 2: P3 "15m rejected prior poc up" (a standing scenario: its line fired "whatever its range, volume and close") -> TAKE if its reads compose at the close | PASS if compose_check refuses it; reads: "15m rejected prior poc up". You were sure of this plan and wrote that you would take it. By the close price ran 30 points up, away from the plan's limit, and compose_check at the close refused it: R:R under the minimum. Confirm or pass?
questions.rule: a standing scenario whose entry ran away: compose_check refuses, so pass; the plan's TAKE and its limit are no reason to take
questions.anchor: PASS if compose_check refuses it.

questions.text: Prepare ahead is on. The briefing's Setups to check: "15m rejected prior poc up" (long; setup candle: hammer, close top third); the setup still stands: no confirming read needed. The trend rule allows a long. Your plan said: scenario 2: P3 "15m rejected prior poc up" (a standing scenario: its line fired "whatever its range, volume and close") -> TAKE if its reads compose at the close | PASS if compose_check refuses it; reads: "15m rejected prior poc up". The closing 3m closed back below the prior POC, still above the 15m setup candle's low. Is that 3m close by itself a reason to pass?
questions.rule: a standing scenario: read the closing candle as candle-reading does (a read, never a veto; the 3m only times the entry): context to weigh, never a pass by itself, never ignored
questions.anchor: read that candle as candle-reading does

questions.text: Price traded a few ticks below the prior RTH low and closed back above it. Per levels-and-reactions, is that a rejection or an acceptance?
questions.rule: traded through and closed back is a rejection
questions.anchor: rejection: traded through, closed back

questions.text: Price is 1.5 ATR below the prior value area high and has not reached it. Has the level rejected price?
questions.rule: not reached means no reaction; no reaction is not a rejection
questions.anchor: No reaction is not a rejection

questions.text: A 15m candle closes above the prior RTH high and the next 15m candle also closes above it. Rejection or acceptance?
questions.rule: closes beyond that hold: acceptance, not a rejection
questions.anchor: acceptance: closes beyond that hold

questions.text: A wick trades above the last confirmed 15m swing high and the candle closes back below it. Is that a BOS?
questions.rule: a wick through a swing that closes back inside is a sweep, not a break
questions.anchor: A wick through a swing that closes back inside is a sweep

questions.text: The 15m is in an uptrend and prints its first close below the last confirmed swing low. BOS or CHoCH, and has the trend reversed?
questions.rule: the first close against the last swing is a CHoCH, an early warning, not a reversal by itself
questions.anchor: the first close beyond the last swing against it

questions.text: The 4h and 1h range, the 15m is up, the 3m regime is trend-up (ADX 24) and the overnight range broke out upward, but the close is 0.4 ATR under the RTH VWAP (EMA20 and the day's move above 0). Has the trend declared itself long?
questions.rule: not declared: all four your way (regime with; RTH VWAP, EMA20 and day's move each above 0); the overnight range is not part of it
questions.anchor: RTH VWAP, EMA20 and day's move each above 0; the overnight range is not part of it

questions.text: The 3m regime is transition (ADX 19), the 15m trend reads up and the 15m just printed a CHoCH down. Per trend-vs-range, what is the 15m: trend, range or transition?
questions.rule: transition: regime and structure disagree
questions.anchor: regime and structure disagree

questions.text: ADX is 16, price crossed the session VWAP 6 times in the last 30 bars, swings are mixed and the last two 15m breaks alternate up and down. Trend or range?
questions.rule: range: neither, and ADX under 18 or 5 or more crosses
questions.anchor: ADX under 18 or 5 or more crosses

questions.text: A 3m range forms inside a 15m uptrend. Is the market ranging?
questions.rule: a 3m range inside a 15m trend is a pause
questions.anchor: A 3m range inside a 15m trend is a pause

questions.text: The 4h and 1h are up and intact. The 15m prints a CHoCH down. Pullback or reversal?
questions.rule: a 15m CHoCH inside an intact 1h and 4h structure is a pullback
questions.anchor: intact 1h and 4h structure is a pullback

questions.text: The 15m CHoCH down is followed by a 1h CHoCH down; the 15m swing low is broken; the down bars are wide on rising volume. A long is offered. Pullback or reversal, and what does it mean for the long?
questions.rule: a reversal developing; the 1h CHoCH against is decisive: pass
questions.anchor: the 1h CHoCH against is decisive

questions.text: The 15m retraced 50% of the leg. Is depth alone a reason to take the long?
questions.rule: depth alone is no edge
questions.anchor: depth alone is no

questions.text: You hold a long. The 15m push failed to make a new high and the pushes are fading, but there is no 15m break against. Reversal?
questions.rule: weakening (two signs), not a reversal without a 15m break
questions.anchor: no 15m break -> weakening

questions.text: Phase 1 reads the journal: the account is tradable, no daily limit, cooldown, floor, blackout or entry block applies, and a lesson from three weeks ago says "target-leg cancel: its cause is not journaled, and no lift appears". May phase 1 base a stand-down on that lesson alone?
questions.rule: a phase-1 stand-down rests only on the account's facts and the stops on them (strategy-library, the priority order's step 1); a lesson is advice, a read in the count, never the reason to pass
questions.anchor: Never on a lesson, a review's notes or earlier reasoning: a lesson is advice
required: \baccount\b|\bhard[- ]stops?\b|\bstops on them\b|\badvice\b|\bweigh\w*|\bthe count\b|\ba read\b|\brule or a block\b|\bgate\b|\brulebook\b|\bnot\b[^.;]*\blessons?\b|\blessons?\b[^.;]*\b(?:not|never|only)\b

questions.text:
Briefing lines (synthetic, 11:36 ET):
- Bias: no side yet (15m range).
- Alignment: long mixed, short mixed. Regime: range, normal volatility.
- Day so far (42 3m bars; `day-context`): rotational: efficiency 0.03 (x sqrt(bars) 0.19), RTH VWAP crosses 11, range 4.1 x 3m ATR(14), net up (its size: Trend declared? day's move); IB day type: today.dayType.
- Rotation evidence (values, not a verdict): RTH VWAP crosses in the last 30 bars 7 (the VWAP line's count); IB day type inside the initial balance; 15m setup candle neither, 3m entry candle neither; failed break (swept the previous high or low, closed back inside): 3m no, 5m unknown, 15m no.
How is the morning so far, in day-context's words, and do these lines show chop evidence, trend evidence, conflicting, or no read yet? Start with one of those four.
questions.rule: chop evidence (class B): the Day so far reads rotational, said "rotating so far"; the IB, the 15m range and the crosses agree
questions.anchor: say it in your read ("trending down so far", "rotating so far", "mixed so far")

questions.text:

- MNQ day: opened 20100 inside the prior value area, gap -6.5 from the prior close (0.03 ADR); prior day 19980-20180, close 20106.5, value area 20050-20140 (POC 20110); overnight 20070-20125; opening type open-auction; initial balance 20062.5-20137.5 (75 points, 0.31 ADR), extended 0 up and 0 down: inside the initial balance; range so far 75 of a 10-day average 240 (31% used).

The last close, 20101, is in the middle of the initial balance. What does day-context call this day, and do these lines show chop evidence, trend evidence, conflicting, or no read yet? Start with one of those four.

questions.anchor: an open inside the prior value area that stays inside the IB is balance

questions.text:
Briefing lines (synthetic, 11:30 ET):
- Bias: long only (4h up, 1h up; short refused).
- Alignment: long aligned, short counter. Regime: trend-up, normal volatility.
- Day so far (40 3m bars; `day-context`): directional up: efficiency 0.3 (x sqrt(bars) 1.9), RTH VWAP crosses 1, range 8.6 x 3m ATR(14), net up (its size: Trend declared? day's move); IB day type: today.dayType.
- Trend declared? (in 3m ATR(14), + = the side's way; `trend-vs-range`): long RTH VWAP +1.8, EMA20 +1.2, overnight range broke out its way, day's move +4.9, regime with; short RTH VWAP -1.8, EMA20 -1.2, overnight range broke out against, day's move -4.9, regime against.
- Rotation evidence (values, not a verdict): RTH VWAP crosses in the last 30 bars 0 (the VWAP line's count); IB day type trend up; 15m setup candle neither, 3m entry candle neither; failed break (swept the previous high or low, closed back inside): 3m no, 5m unknown, 15m no.
